name: plf::colony (plf::hive)
workload: Independent microbenchmark suite (fill/back-insertion, linear search, random insert, randomized iterate-and-erase at 1%/50% erasure probability, sort, destruction) across element sizes from 8B to 4096B on GCC/libstdc++.
claimed_speedup: "three orders of magnitude faster than the vector and deque" at 1% random erasure with 1024B elements; "about 361'143 times faster than the vector" at 50% random erasure with large elements (verbatim from post); colony reported ~3x SLOWER than std::vector-with-reserve for simple 32B fill/back-insertion.
tradeoffs: Unordered container: element insertion order is not preserved and elements are not indexable by position like vector's operator[]; higher per-element memory overhead (skip-field metadata) than vector; key advantage is that erase() never invalidates other iterators/pointers/references (unlike vector/deque), which is what makes bulk random erasure O(1) per element instead of O(n).
caveats: Benchmark dated 2017 on GCC 4.9.4 (dated compiler); the headline 361,143x figure is specific to a 50%-random-erasure iterate/erase workload on large (multi-KB) elements at whatever container size the author's graph reached, and reflects colony's O(1) erase vs. vector/deque's O(n) erase-and-shift -- an asymptotic-complexity artifact, not a representative 'typical workload' multiplier; for simple sequential fill of small/medium elements the same post reports colony as slower than std::vector. Only libstdc++ (GCC) was exercised in this post, not libc++ or MSVC STL. The library's own site (plflib.org/colony.htm, colony v6.11, GCC 9.2 x64, Intel Xeon E3-1241 Haswell, -O2 -march=native, benchmark source in the colony downloads section) shows qualitatively consistent rankings (colony/list leading insertion and erasure, vector leading iteration) but presents numbers as graph images rather than machine-readable text, so it was used only as corroboration, not the primary citation. The library has since been forked/renamed to plf::hive (github.com/mattreecebentley/plf_hive, 179 stars, also active) to track the pending std::hive standardization proposal (P0447); both repos are maintained in parallel by the same author and the cited benchmark evidence applies to both implementations.
found_via: Blogs / talks (CppCon, C++Now, Meeting C++, C++ on Sea, personal engineering blogs): HN Algolia search for "plf colony container" surfaced Baptiste Wicht's blog post "C++ Containers Benchmark: vector/list/deque and plf::colony" (baptiste-wicht.com, May 2017), cross-checked against plflib.org/colony.htm.
